method: each prompt planned by two fresh read-only reviewer subagents: with the skill (told to read it) and baseline (told not to read .claude/skills/); assertions graded by the planner from the returned plans

results.note: both chose to change existing owners, not a new skill; the baseline added a tested --refresh flag, the skill run a procedure edit with no test
the baseline invented a parallel config/demo_pieces.yaml + demo_gate.py; the skill run extended test_matrix.py
only the skill run put real incident gotchas in the new skill (summed debug+release counts 412fd74, reviews.log before merge, WAIVED wording)

verdict: lands: small but consistent gain on the judgement path; the baseline is already strong because SKILL_POLICY and AGENTS.md carry the script-first rule
caveat: baseline runs can see the AGENTS.md line naming .claude/skills/ (added in the same change), so the format assertion is not a clean contrast
